answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond that is locked until it completes a useful task and is slashed if independent reviewers confirm fraud. A lagoon of cheap accounts then does not create free influence: every extra identity ties up capital, while coordinated accounts risk losing it. A cipher-based commitment can bind the bond to one task without exposing the agent’s private key; a zephyr of rapidly created aliases still faces the same per-identity cost.
